text: What the engine does EETE takes the details of a job offer and a candidate's own situation and works out what the offer really costs and really pays: after tax, after commute, after every mandatory cost the job imposes on daily life. It produces a plain signal, shows the numbers and what would change them, and stops there. It is not financial, tax, legal or employment advice. Gross-to-net position What the offer pays before tax, and what actually lands after PAYE, UIF and retirement and medical deductions. Mandatory cost load Costs this specific job imposes: commute, a required wardrobe, self-supplied technology, location-driven housing. Never generic lifestyle spending. Effective hourly rate Net pay divided by the real hours the job takes, commute included. Equal salaries can differ sharply here. The signal Accept, caution or reject: a plain read of whether the numbers clear the published thresholds, the same for every candidate, every time. Cash surplus Money in minus money out: the number a bank balance would show. Economic surplus One step further: it also counts the value of the person's own time. A job can be cash-positive every month and still economically negative once you count how much of a life it takes.
title: EETE

tags: L0–L7, one domain end to end
text: One calculation, five readers Every report comes from the same underlying calculation, rendered for the person reading it. Nobody gets a different number; some readers get less detail. Report For What it shows Candidate Report The candidate Their own economics, resilience, role fit and relocation impact, never the employer's internal assessment of them Offer Defensibility Report The recruiter presenting the offer The full hiring picture: cost of acceptance, churn risk, market context and business justification, alongside the candidate's economics Total Cost of Employment Audit HR, rewards and the hiring manager The same internal picture as the recruiter's report Regulatory Compliance Summary A regulator or auditor Process evidence: decision trace, signal confidence, version and hash integrity, with no granular personal-financial detail Legal Preparation Record Legal, for dispute preparation Every section: the fullest record available Every report carries a decision-reasons section drawn only from figures already on the page. If a recruiter or employer decides differently from the signal, the report says so and records the reason they gave, so nobody reads a decision without knowing whether a person overrode the numbers. Each report also carries a right of reply.
title: EETE

tags: L0–L7, one domain end to end
text: Six standing positions What the platform does and doesn't do, held in the code rather than in a policy document. No protected attributes Race, gender, disability, marital status, religion, health and credit or criminal-record data don't exist in the domain model. That's structural isolation, not a filter applied late. A human always decides The single autonomous mechanism only routes a report to a faster or more thorough review. It never issues a decision, and human overrides are disclosed on the report. Issued records are immutable Every report carries a cryptographic fingerprint anyone can recompute. A changed input produces a new report linked to the one it supersedes, never a silent edit. No bare numbers Every point estimate carries a range, robustness or sensitivity read. No module infers beyond structured input, and each states what it doesn't invent. Personal information protected The scanner sees only what it is explicitly given. Pilots run under a written operator agreement under POPIA, with purpose-limited processing and deletion on request. Real deletion A delete actually deletes. Only a minimal audit row with no personal information may remain, and nothing is presented as deleted when it isn't.
title: EETE

tags: L0–L7, one domain end to end
text: Built as a data product The engine's real asset is its contract: a typed calculation request in, a typed result out, exported as versioned JSON Schema. Integrations are built against the schema, never against source code, and input and output hashes give every result its lineage. Model the input, optional with a sensible default, so existing requests keep validating. Model the output, with a plain statement of what it computed from and what it deliberately did not invent. Write a pure function that never fabricates a value; a missing signal is reported as missing. Wire it into the pipeline before the result is hashed. Bump the engine version, minor for anything additive. Test every load-bearing branch, not just that it runs. Expose it in the console if a reader needs to see it. Document it wherever it touches personal information or compliance. Verify it for real: tests, lint and schema export, then a live click-through.

text: The problem An employment offer is one of the most consequential decisions an organisation makes and one of the least documented. It is judged from the employer's side only, so offers that look affordable on paper fail in month four.
title: The Employer Report

text: Nkosinathi Mbambo Spine build · Engineer Raw to Gold, and Back A two-leg platform: a DuckLake lakehouse for evidence and a Postgres lakebase for action, joined by metadata-driven master data. Status Phase 1 in build Lead demand Engineer · Solutionist posture Spine plane L1 Evidence · L2 Identity Method stage Discover · Connect Repository Ingqiqo/raw-to-gold · opening soon
title: Raw to Gold, and Back

text: What it gives you If you want analytics and operations to run on the same truth, not two copies that drift, A lakehouse for evidence and a lakebase for action, joined by master data, so what you analyse is what you act on.
title: Raw to Gold, and Back

text: The problem Most data platforms move bytes well and meaning badly. By the gold layer nobody can say which definition a number used or who changed it, and the operational systems that act on the numbers disagree about who a customer even is.
title: Raw to Gold, and Back

text: Approach Run the lakehouse leg on DuckLake as a data mesh: each domain, modelled with domain-driven design, owns its Bronze-to-Gold slice, and a logical data fabric virtualises access across domains. Land Bronze raw and immutable; model Silver as Data Vault 2.0; compile Gold into multi-format, poly-database projections from ledger tables: general, relationship, causal and event graphs, time series and dimensional models. Ingest with dlt and Airbyte, stream with Arroyo, extract documents with Unstructured.io, transform with dbt on DuckDB, and gate every tier with ODCS data contracts, Soda Core, YData Profiling, Pydantic v2 and pytest. Bridge to the lakebase leg, Postgres for applications with Polars on the app side, through multi-domain master data: Zingg matching driven by ontology metadata into AtroCore, with DuckDB, dlt and Airbyte carrying reverse ETL. Share one semantic layer between DuckDB and Polars, expose lakehouse metadata to other engines through Apache XTable, and trace every hop in DataHub with OpenLineage.
